summary: State-run 60 ft steel tower on Okemo Mountain, Vermont; register dates the first wooden tower to 1924, a 1922 item says it was being built; 2025 maintenance and railings.

facts.design: 60-foot steel fire tower (steel construction), replacing a wooden tower about 30 ft tall
facts.agency: Vermont Department of Forest, Parks and Recreation

staffing.status: fire wardens posted at the tower into the autumn in 1934 and 1963 items; current staffing not in the sources read

access.note: The state forest page describes the paved Okemo Mountain Road as reaching the summit and the refurbished tower as a summit feature. A 2025 state press release expected shorter closures during railing work.

visit.trail_note: The 3-mile Healdville Trail runs from the base to the summit. The state points visitors to Trail Finder for closure updates. The sources read do not state climbing rules for the cab.

events.note: State acquired two acres at the summit of Ludlow Mountain in Mount Holly (register)
Burlington Free Press (Oct. 18, 1922) says a fire lookout tower was being erected on Ludlow Mountain; conflicts with the register's 1924 build date
Register: original wooden tower built with help from the Okemo Mountain Club, 30 ft tall
CCC work on the new steel tower began (register); a 1934 item says a CCC company would camp on the mountain to build it
Fire warden Lindsey S. Hall located at the tower until November 1 (Rutland Daily Herald item)
New 60-foot steel tower completed around 1937 (register), replacing a wooden tower of half that height (Rutland Daily Herald, Sept. 16, 1937)
Watchman's cabin built 100 feet from the tower (register)
Three-room warden's cabin at the base of the tower completely removed (register)
Stone chimney built in 1951 for the lookout cabin; it is all that remains of that cabin (register). The register does not say whether the lookout cabin is the 1943 watchman's cabin
October 1963 item: a man planned to stay at the tower until the first week of November

Register: contractor painted the stairway, replaced 10 steps, installed ground wires, a railing in the tower cab, reinforced the landing floors and a chain link fence along the stairs and landings; a stairway upgrade is also noted in the Forest Lookouts history
New steel plate roof installed, thanks to Okemo Mountain Resort (register)
Tower maintenance completed at Okemo, Burke and Bear Hill: lightning protection, paint, interior cab railings, wire mesh on stairs and landings (condition report)
State planned safety railings for this tower with a $60,000 Recreational Trails Program share, work extending into spring 2026 (press release dated April 30, 2025)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1924 for the first wooden tower. A Burlington Free Press item of October 18, 1922 says a tower was being erected that year. Both are reported.
The register and 1922 items say Ludlow Mountain; the state forest page and 1928 items say Okemo Mountain. Treated as the same summit.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 2010 're-wooded' wording is not in the register text read (corrected). Not verified in pages read: the 2012 'ski area workers' and certificate detail, and the June 19, 2023 NHLR registration date (the grep did not return the date line), so neither is in the story. Climbing rules for the cab are not stated in the sources read; the state page implies public visits. Build date conflicts (1922/1924) and the summit-name conflict are reported in the story. Fact-check 2026-10-08: story now says the state describes spectacular 360-degree views, attributes the 1951 chimney to the register's lookout cabin and flags that the register does not say it is the watchman's cabin, and footnotes the wood sentence. Pages read: 8, over the 6-page budget because the NHLR and Eastern pages are long.
